criteria.adapter_held_service: Land the full behavior now, locally: duplicate the K06 engine into the i03 runtime slice verbatim, instantiate it inside the adapter factory next to the shared test owner, and project each engine method as an owner-first late:: catalogue operation under a fresh NT-I03 admission tag with row-level owner elision. Engine rejections become typed Can failures through a two-family mapping (lookup-class kinds to test::stale_handle, everything else to late::late_fault carrying kind plus reason). Ship Can vocabulary helpers, per-operation wrappers, and a small end-to-end example exercising selection through outcome. Provisional until P14 like every I slice; the I04 adapter-held doubles are the direct ancestor of this shape.
criteria.defer_mechanics_inert_facts: Land shapes without behavior: add the late:: fact records and vocabulary predicates to the catalogue and Can helpers, keep all twelve engine methods out of the candidate surface, and leave LateOccurrenceService as a host-executed tool. Executable occurrences and leases then enter the candidate only through their dedicated future merges (P09 workspace leases, P11 recovery gating), so no interim double ever impersonates them. This is the conservative reading of the I02 witness precedent applied to the whole K06 engine rather than only its stateful half.
criteria.external_n_dispatch: Land the operation surface with postponed semantics: publish owner-first late:: operations whose adapter implementation builds N-owner envelopes and awaits injected dispatch that rejects until P14 qualifies the owner. Engine state (identities, enrollments, gates, sequences, terminals, leases, counters) will reside in N; the candidate holds no copy. Can vocabulary, wrappers, and the example mirror the I01/I11 structure. Staging cost is minimal and no local double can drift from the future authority, at the price that every late call fails loudly until the owner arrives.

i03_late_staging_decision.instructions: Stage the I03 late-events merge. Three stagings compete: run the accepted K06 engine inside the candidate adapter now; publish the operation surface now with the engine living in the future N owner; or publish only inert fact shapes and vocabularies now with all execution deferred to the true P09/P11 owners. The engine is self-contained deterministic mechanics (gated two-participant occurrences, terminal-bound leases, death-aware outcomes) with closed vocabularies (terminals completed/rejected/failed), hard caps, and 30 green checks; it deliberately mirrors P09/P11 wording while remaining local. The codebase already contains both staging ancestors: adapter-held doubles (I04) and throw-until-N dispatch (I01, I11), plus a no-operations host-side witness (I02/K05). I03 requires catalogue growth with Can helpers and an example, and must stay provisional while P14 is blocked. Which staging best serves a truthful, reviewable, confusion-free merge?
